issues.description: The UML in problem_statement.md declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) with a void return type (lines 16-19), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(int) returning boolean. This return-type mismatch between the specification and the provided solution/implementations will confuse students about the expected method signature and may cause compilation or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Pneumatic interface return type across artifacts. Either update problem_statement.md and the UML to specify boolean as the return type for raisePressure(int), or (preferably) change the Pneumatic interface in the solution and template to declare void raisePressure(int) and adjust the implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) accordingly so all artifacts use the same signature.

issues.description: The UML in problem_statement.md defines Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int): void, but the solution repository declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) returning boolean. The implementing classes in the solution (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) use a void return for raisePressure, creating an internal mismatch in the solution and a conflict with the UML. This discrepancy will confuse students: the problem statement/UML indicate a void method, template expects them to declare the abstract methods accordingly, but the solution's interface uses a different return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.raisePressure signature consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution interface to declare void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) to match the UML/problem statement and match the implementing classes, or update the UML/problem statement to specify a boolean return type and adjust the template and implementing classes accordingly. Prefer changing the solution interface to void to align with the UML and template expectations.
